headline: Sequence foundation models are specialized by pretraining scope, input encoding, readout and design objectives
label: Task Aware Pretrained Sequence Models
summary: Nine new works tailor DNA and RNA language models to specific tasks via clade-specific pretraining, modified inputs, region-aware readouts and oracle-guided design.
synthesis: The common thread is moving DNA and RNA language models away from generic embeddings toward task-specific specialization. Several works modify inputs or readouts: ModBERT encodes variants and CpG methylation in a five-letter genome, the mRNA study averages embeddings separately over 5' UTR, CDS and 3' UTR, and MARRI adds opening penalties and hybridization gains to cross-RNA attention. Others alter pretraining scope or conditioning: an apicomplexan-specific GPN trained on 455 assemblies improves P. falciparum epigenomic prediction, B-RANKO is a 150M-parameter bidirectional decoder-only ncRNA model, and GenNA conditions generation on natural-language annotations. GENECraft and REGAL pair sequence models with functional oracles for controllable regulatory DNA and enhancer design. Fine-tuned Borzoi and AlphaGenome match variant-based linear models in admixed genomes, indicating limits to the gains from adaptation.
